summary:
Junior Astronaut: Journey Beyond Earth is a bilingual (English/Thai) Roblox experience that lets young players live the path from dreaming about space to working on the Moon. Players watch a fictional space-agency recruitment broadcast, apply with their own dream, then train through a fitness test, an underwater EVA pool drill inspired by NASA’s Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory, and a cadet exam. They then fly to the Moon for a multi-step mission: restoring life support, growing food, sealing an airlock, sheltering in a solar storm drill and sending a report to Earth. The mission ends with a flag-raising, a personalized certificate and a family homecoming.

It addresses the challenge by turning passive STEM learning into hands-on decisions. Power must be rationed, plants need light, water and nutrients, and airlock pressure must match before a hatch opens. Wrong choices give hints and a retry, so children learn without being punished.

It matters because space can feel like someone else’s job. By letting kids apply, train and succeed as an astronaut, the game builds curiosity, confidence and early interest in science, in both English and Thai. Mission 1 is the Moon; Mars and more destinations are planned. Created with AI assistance (Claude, Gemini, Codex) and reviewed by the team. This is an independent project, not affiliated with NASA.
details:
What it does. Junior Astronaut: Journey Beyond Earth is a Roblox experience where a child lives the path to becoming an astronaut. The player watches a fictional space-agency recruitment news broadcast in a galaxy-themed bedroom and submits an application with their own dream. At a training center inspired by NASA’s Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory, they complete a left-right treadmill sprint, three underwater EVA pool drills (tether, handrail, repair panel), four knowledge boards and a cadet exam (pass 4 of 5). Then they fly to the Moon for a multi-step base mission:

  • build the air system
  • grow and harvest food
  • seal an airlock and match pressure
  • aim a dish to reach Earth
  • handle a loss of sunlight
  • shelter during a solar storm drill

The game ends with a flag-raising and a family homecoming with a mission diary. A golden path and objective bar guide the player, and wrong answers explain why and allow a retry.

Benefits and impact. Power rationing, plant needs, airlock safety and teamwork become decisions instead of facts to memorize. The whole game switches between English and Thai in one tap, so Thai children can learn space in their own language. We want children to see themselves in space careers. The level-select screen already shows Mars as the next mission.

Tools. Roblox Studio, Lua/Luau (server and client scripts, UI, cutscenes) and the Roblox Creator Store. AI assistants (Claude, Gemini, Codex) helped with code, text, visual design and slides. All AI-assisted work was reviewed and tested by the team. Space facts come from NASA pages listed in the NASA Data section.

Creativity. The player is the character, not a viewer. Their own dream appears in the news screen, Noel’s dialogue and the diary. Every science idea is a mini-game, such as splitting limited battery power or matching airlock pressure.

Factors considered.

  • Kid-friendly language and no punishment for mistakes
  • Bilingual play
  • Chat filtering of the player’s typed dream
  • Sparking curiosity: the game is a first step, not the end. Each lesson ends with a simple “why,” so players want to ask more questions and keep exploring space on their own, for example with NASA’s kid-friendly pages (NASA Space Place). We chose short, playable lessons over long explanations so children finish the game wanting to learn more.
  • Roblox currently labels new games 16+ until they have enough players. We plan to open the game to younger players once that is lifted.

Gameplay is a simplified simulation inspired by real NASA concepts. This is an independent project and is not affiliated with NASA. It uses no NASA logos.
